items_missed: No 'How are you today?' — went straight from greeting to 'Can I have your first and last name'
No agenda statement and no 'Sound good?' confirmation — never told Jameson the call would take 10-15 minutes or what the structure would be
Never asked about stairs or floors at the ORIGIN (a house he shares with roommates) — only established the third-floor destination
Never asked about additional rooms — garage, storage unit, balcony, patio
No special-considerations probe — long walk from truck to elevator, narrow hallways, tight turns, parking at the apartment
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — the $2,000 accidental damage coverage was completely absent
Meet Your Mover never mentioned (movers 'will give you a call once they're on the way' is not the pre-move email with mover photo)
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — she gave a 1PM-3PM ETA window but no promise to start discounting if it's missed
Incomplete what's-included list — named truck, blankets, shrink wrap, bands, dollies, tools but not gas, taxes, or insurance
Incomplete no-hidden-fees pitch — 'no credit card fees, no [travel] fees, no disassemble or reassembly fees' but no fuel surcharge callout
Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips, no 'take a carload,' no link between prep and a shorter/cheaper move, despite a 3-hour job where 30 minutes of prep is real money
No mention of the BOLDED detail list at the top of the confirmation email or 'reply with any corrections' — just 'I will send you the confirmation email'
Gave 'don't hesitate to call back' but never stated business hours or how to reach the team
No insurance explanation at all — neither No Worries nor the 60c/lb baseline
Walk distance never raised as a time variable on a third-floor apartment move
No equivalents/visual reference (school bus, etc.) used to frame truck capacity or time
top_strength: The estimate build was genuinely well-constructed: she laid out all three day-of-week rates unprompted, flagged Sunday as the cheapest option in the customer's interest, then named the third-floor unit as the specific reason to budget 3 to 3.5 hours and gave a real dollar range ($666-$777) rather than a single number.
coaching_note: Amy sold the price well and skipped everything that protects the price. On a 3-hour, $666-$777 Saturday job with a third-floor walk-up-by-elevator, the Save Your Ass speech is the single highest-leverage 60 seconds on the call and she gave zero of it — no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload,' no connection between prep and a shorter bill. Add to that: No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee were all absent, so a repeat customer who already likes Einstein got no reason to believe Einstein is better than the next quote. Her own instinct is the fix — she asked 'what are your biggest concerns?' and he told her the date was the whole issue, then she talked past his stated Saturday preference ('so let's just do Friday then... Or Saturday') and had to self-correct. Slow down at the two moments that matter: confirm the date he actually picked, then run the prep speech before you send the email.
phone_presence_notes: Real warmth in spots — congratulating him on the fiancee and 'a new chapter,' plus 'Amazing' and 'Perfect' on the booking — but stretches of mechanical, stumbling delivery (repeated 'do we have any additional stop,' the Friday/Saturday mix-up, several garbled price restatements) kept it transactional overall.
audio_review_reason: Heavy transcription garbling around the rate and estimate figures ('$216,216 per hour', '$666,123 is $777', 'no terrible', 'for Revers') makes it unclear whether Amy actually misspoke the numbers to the customer or the transcript mangled clean speech — that distinction changes the clarity/pace score in Section 9.
